title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Rises 0.4% to $508.29 (Nov 18)
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) closed at $508.29 on Nov 18, up 0.40% in line with the Nasdaq, as Satya Nadella spoke at DealBook and Microsoft explained its outage.
body_markdown:
## Why Microsoft Stock Rose


No news source reviewed for this article tied Microsoft's 0.40% gain to a company-specific announcement, and the move tracked the Nasdaq's 0.42% rise. Three Microsoft items surfaced around the session.


On Wednesday, Nadella spoke onstage at the DealBook Summit about Nvidia, where Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive the week before after 33 years in the role. According to[TechCrunch](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/microsoft-ceo-satya-nadella-remains-231728146.html) , Nadella said, "I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work," and called interim CEO Colette Kress, a former Microsoft employee, "a tremendous person."


Also on Wednesday, Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna explained the November 12 outage that took down several Microsoft 365 services. As reported by[SlashGear](https://www.slashgear.com/2320849/microsoft-november-2026-outage-cause-explained/) , Lamanna traced it in a post on X to a "latent defect" introduced in an earlier fix to a Microsoft 365 networking gateway server, which turned into a "cascading failure" when Teams traffic was switched to a backup network. Engineers restored service by applying a hotfix and restarting servers in batches.


In a report published after the close,[Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/billionaire-bill-ackman-sold-2-224231574.html) noted that Pershing Square's quarterly 13F filing showed 4,064,779 Microsoft shares on September 30, down from 6,206,730 three months earlier. Bill Ackman disclosed on X that the fund also holds 2 million deep-in-the-money Microsoft options bought over the counter in July, which the filing does not capture.


## MSFT Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Outage cause identified: a Microsoft executive has publicly traced the November 12 outage to a specific defect and described the hotfix and restart steps, per SlashGear.
- Large holder exposure: counting the over-the-counter options, Pershing Square holds about 4.1 million Microsoft shares plus options on 2 million more, versus 6.2 million shares in June, according to Motley Fool.
- Session recovery: the stock climbed back from its intraday low to close $7.21 above it, finishing in line with the Nasdaq Composite.


### Risks


- Service reliability: SlashGear reports the defect stayed dormant under normal loads, activated on newer servers with more cores, and spread because the shard barriers meant to isolate failures did not hold.
- Mixed market backdrop: the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.32% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.23% in the same session, even as the Nasdaq rose.
- Distance from the high: the stock closed 9.10% below its 52-week high after a session on below-average volume.

## How MSFT Traded in the Session


After opening at $505.50, Microsoft dipped to an intraday low of $501.08, then recovered to finish $7.21 above that low. Trading was lighter than usual, with volume running 12.04% below its average.


The gain matched the broader technology tape. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42% to 24,429.88, leaving Microsoft 0.02 percentage points behind the index, while the[S&P 500](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/sp-500-what-it-is-and-what-really-moves-it/) slipped 0.23% to 7,323.63 and the[Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/dow-jones-industrial-average-djia-explained/) fell 1.32% to 50,089.71. The US 10-year Treasury yield eased 3.0 basis points to 5.07%.


Large technology peers were split.[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) climbed 3.82% to $267.74 and[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) added 0.80%, while Apple rose 0.15%, Meta Platforms slipped 0.40% and[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) fell 2.89% to $150.96. Microsoft ended the session 9.10% below its 52-week high and 45.56% above its 52-week low.
